steps.title: Where to start: write out the factors
steps.body: The big $\Pi$ means product: it works like a sum sign, but you multiply the terms instead of adding them. Here $i$ runs from $1$ to $10$, so there are ten factors. When a product has a pattern like $\frac{i}{i+1}$, writing out a few factors is the fastest way to see what cancels.

steps.title: Look for cancelling
steps.body:
The whole product is
$$\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{3}{4}\cdots\frac{9}{10}\cdot\frac{10}{11}$$
The denominator of each factor is the same as the numerator of the next factor, so they cancel in pairs. This is called telescoping: the product collapses like a folding telescope.

your_turn.answer: $\frac{1}{3}$. The $2$ on the bottom of the first factor cancels the $2$ on top of the second.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Every number from $2$ to $10$ appears once on top and once on the bottom, so all of them cancel. Only the first numerator, $1$, and the last denominator, $11$, are left. Careful: the last denominator is $10 + 1 = 11$, not $10$. The answer is **$\frac{1}{11}$**.
